business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid civil law system based on the Napoleonic and Egyptian codes, with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation, supplemented by specialised investment, financial and AML/CFT regulations from GAFI, the Financial Regulatory Authority and the Central Bank of Egypt
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (BIT)
Egypt–Germany Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (BIT)
Egypt–France Agreement on the Reciprocal Protection of Investments (BIT)
Egypt–Netherlands Agreement on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
Unified Agreement for Investment of Capital in Arab Countries (Arab League, 1980, as amended)
Egypt–United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement
Egypt–Saudi Arabia Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009; Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) and Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017 as amended); Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014, Law No. 8 of 2015 and Law No. 106 of 2020; Executive Regulations of the AML Law issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 17 of 2003 as amended; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations; Financial Regulatory Authority beneficial ownership and AML rules; Unified Tax Law No. 91 of 2005.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Commercial Registry Extract of the ultimate parent or foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry (e.g. UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Amsterdam Chamber of Commerce) or the Egyptian Commercial Registry if the shareholder is Egyptian
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a contracting party to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Egyptian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (constitutional documents) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or competent corporate registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in the country of origin, then Hague Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization depending on the Hague Convention status of the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorising the formation of the Egypt LLC, appointment of its first manager and registered agent, and approval of the UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notary certification followed by Hague Apostille; or Egyptian Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian registered agent / counsel to complete the incorporation and sign statutory filings in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder acting through an authorised signatory, notarised before a competent foreign notary public or the Egyptian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian Consular Legalization after notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport bio-pages and proof of residence address for each ultimate beneficial owner, director, manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority, foreign notary public, or Egyptian Public Notary for certified copies made in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign-issued documents; Egyptian Notary Public certification for copies certified inside Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and letter of good standing from the corporate shareholder's bank relating to the proposed Egyptian investment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consularly legalized where the bank's home jurisdiction requires authentication before submission to GAFI

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, authorized signatories, and any person exercising direct or indirect control over the Egyptian LLC against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK OFSI consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Egyptian terrorist designation lists issued under Law No. 80 of 2002 / Law No. 106 of 2020, CBE domestic watchlists, and integrity databases including the World Bank Debarment List and Interpol Red Notices. Screening must include fuzzy name matching and Arabic/Latin transliteration matching, date-of-birth and nationality verification, PEP status determination covering domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and close associates, enhanced due diligence for higher-risk jurisdictions, non-face-to-face incorporation instructions, shell corporate structures, and transactions involving virtual assets or cash-intensive businesses. Any unresolved sanctions hit or PEP red flag must result in refusal, filing of a suspicious activity report with the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit, and retention of all CDD/EDD records for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_program_designation: A licensed corporate service provider performing registered-agent and offshore-secretarial functions must designate a board-level compliance officer and an MLRO qualified under Egyptian law, implement risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence procedures, and maintain a written AML/CFT programme approved by GAFI and the AML/CFT Unit.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.educational_licensing_note: Egypt does not maintain a standalone Category A statutory licensing regime for trust or company service providers equivalent to the UK TCSP; however, the provision of company secretarial services is regulated under the Companies Law and Investment Law and must be carried out by a licensed Egyptian lawyer or a GAFI-licensed corporate service provider whose activities may be examined by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and AML/CFT supervisors.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.regulated_activity_notification: For a foreign parent group, the Egyptian registered-agent subsidiary must notify GAFI and the AML/CFT Unit of its business plan and provide the names, passports and UBO declarations of all founding members and managers at incorporation stage.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pre_incorporation_calendar_risk: The entire pre-incorporation process for a medium-risk corporate secretarial business should be staffed for 20–30 calendar days, including name reservation, apostille/notarization, Arabic translation, GAFI registration, and Egypt Tax Authority registration; any defects in legalization or UBO filings will suspend the 30-day name reservation clock.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.supervisory_information_sharing: As part of pre-incorporation due diligence, GAFI may consult the AML/CFT Unit, the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit and the CBE regarding high-risk beneficial owners or cross-border structures before issuing the certificate of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services Portal / Egyptian Companies Registry online services at www.gafi.gov.eg, operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), together with GAFI Investor Service Centres for in-person name clearance submissions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name of an Egyptian LLC must be written in Arabic characters and correspond to the Arabic names of the members or the company's permitted business purpose. A Latin-script transliteration may be registered as a secondary commercial name using standard Egyptian transliteration rules. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not indicate a business activity outside the approved objects clause, and must avoid any wording that would mislead the public as to nationality, state sponsorship, religious significance or regulatory status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration through the GAFI Investor Services Portal within 15 working days of the electronic rejection notice. The reconsideration must set out the grounds of objection, evidence of uniqueness, and an alternative Arabic and transliterated name. If GAFI maintains its rejection, an appeal may be lodged with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within a further 15 working days. A final administrative appeal may be filed with the GAFI Chairman within 30 days; an adverse final decision may be contested before the Egyptian Administrative Court (State Council) within 60 days. A name reservation that is about to expire while GAFI is processing the incorporation may be extended once for an additional 30 days on submission of the incorporation file and payment of the extension fee.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.statutory_filing_deadline_after_reservat: The LLC incorporation file must be filed with GAFI before the expiry of the 30-day name reservation window; failure to file on time requires a new name reservation and payment of a fresh GAFI search fee.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.translator_and_language_board_sop: Arabic translations of foreign constitutional documents and powers of attorney must be prepared by a sworn translator accredited with the Egyptian Ministry of Justice; the Arabic name transliteration must match the transliteration used on the UBO declaration and commercial registry forms.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office address is not acceptable as the statutory registered office of an Egyptian LLC. For the commercial registered-agent and secretarial business, GAFI will require a physical office in Egypt with substantive presence including rentable premises, letterhead, signage, communications systems and availability during business hours. A serviced office or business centre can satisfy the physical address requirement if it is leased under a valid contract and maintained as the LLC's registered address; however, the company cannot rely on a mail-forwarding or virtual-only provider.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated. Quantified annual risk of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first 12 months is estimated at approximately 30–40%, falling to 10–15% per annum thereafter. The probability increases where the registered-agent business serves multiple offshore entities, high-risk clients, foreign shell structures, or non-face-to-face incorporations from a single address. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit and, where applicable, the CBE may conduct unannounced physical inspections; all corporate records, statutory books and CDD files must be retained at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 149 of 2019, Articles 15, 28, 32, 60-77 (Limited Liability Company provisions); Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 2020; supplementary Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration and Establishment One-Stop-Shop; downstream filing with the Commercial Registry (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Aqd Al-Taasis) and Memorandum of Association filed in Arabic through the GAFI e-Establishment portal; notarized and certified by an Egyptian licensed attorney.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; the share capital is freely set by the partners and must be fully subscribed at incorporation. The cash portion must be deposited into a temporary corporate bank account in Egypt and evidenced by a capital deposit certificate; in-kind contributions require a sworn auditor's valuation report. Capital funds are released to the company upon issuance of the incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) THAT the subscribers hereby form the Company as Egyptian Limited Liability Company named [Company Name] under Law No. 149 of 2019, with issued share capital of EGP [amount] divided into [number] shares, fully subscribed and paid per the capital deposit certificate issued by [Bank]; (2) THAT the registered office shall be at [address], Cairo, Governorate, Arab Republic of Egypt and this address be notified to the Commercial Registry and the General Authority for Investment; (3) THAT [Names] are appointed as Managers with joint/senior signatory powers of the Company and [Name] as Company Secretary; (4) THAT officers are authorized to complete the statutory registration, tax, social insurance and licensing proceedings of the Company. ADOPTED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Economic Activity Code Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI e-Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg) — Trade Name Reservation Unit, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit at least three candidate trade names in Arabic or with a transliterated Latin variant. Declare the intended ISIC 8299 activity as 'Business support and corporate secretarial office services, including acting as registered agent and sub-licensed offshore secretarial facility selection'. GAFI screens the names against the Commercial Registry index and registered trademarks and issues a name reservation certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name reservation online application
List of proposed trade names with Arabic translation
Passport copies of each founding shareholder/member
Power of attorney (if agents execute on behalf of any shareholder)
Declaration of intended ISIC 8299 scope of activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised request with three new variants within 15 days; if similarity disputes arise, petition the GAFI Dispute Resolution Committee or the competent commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Incorporation Contract; Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian attorney/notary and any commercial bank operating in Egypt (temporary capital account).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Partners execute the Incorporation Contract and Memorandum of Association in Arabic before a certified lawyer who files the notarization copy. The appointed manager opens a temporary capital account in a domestic bank and deposits the cash subscription amount; the bank issues a capital deposit certificate noting the depositor, the intended company name and the restricted release condition. If in-kind capital is used, a sworn auditor values the assets in a formal report annexed to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by GAFI
Incorporation Contract and Memorandum of Association (original, Arabic)
Notarization and legalization statements by the certified attorney
Bank capital deposit certificate
Sworn auditor valuation report for in-kind contributions (if any)
Copy of shareholder passports and national IDs
Written consent of each manager and the company secretary to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit certificate due to a defective company name, obtain a corrected deposit certificate or issue a capital re-deposit with a written bank confirmation; re-notarize any corrected contractual schedules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing and GAFI One-Stop-Shop Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (Companies Incorporation Department) — e-filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload and submit the scanned notarized incorporation contract, bank certificate, registered office documentation, manager/sec secretary consents and the activity declaration. GAFI reviews the capital structure, legal compliance, and premises; upon approval, GAFI issues a preliminary certificate of incorporation and forwards an extract for publication. Concurrently apply for the segregation activity code 8299 within the company's registered objects.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Contract and Memorandum of Association (notarized)
Bank capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease or ownership certificate with free-zone or downtown building authorization
Manager and company secretary consent letters with specimen signatures
GAFI standard incorporation form (Arabic)
Approval from the licensed attorney that the contract complies with Law No. 149/2019
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: GAFI may issue a single deficiency query listing required corrections; cure within 30 days by amending the contract and re-submitting before the application lapses. If approval is denied, file written administrative appeal to the GAFI Appeals Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office — Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade (or GAFI on-site window for service companies).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the GAFI preliminary certificate, file an application for commercial registration of the LLC. The registry annotates the company's legal form, capital, managers, registered office, and the ISIC-compatible activity '8299 — corporate secretarial services and registered agent office'. Payment of commercial registration fees and publication of the incorporation extract in the official gazette is completed in this step.
required_dossiers: GAFI preliminary incorporation certificate
Notarized incorporation contract
Capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease/ownership proof
Original power of attorney for filing representatives
Official commercial registry application form (Form 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the application due to discrepancies in the object clause, amend the contract and file a corrective resolution; minor administrative delays are cured by paying a supplemental registry fee and re-submitting within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), and the competent branch of the Ministry of Finance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, apply to the ETA for a Tax Identification Number (registration number) and Tax Card (Kart Damibiyya). Register for VAT if the expected taxable turnover exceeds the threshold; operational corporate secretarial services are subject to 14% VAT eff. 2023. Within 3 months of paying first wages, enroll the company and its employees with NOSI for social insurance contributions.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
GAFI incorporation certificate
Tax card application form (T1) and VAT registration form (T2) if applicable
Copy of contracts, POS receipts or projected turnover declarations
Manager's national ID/passport and proof of office address
Employee count and planned payroll declaration for NOSI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA delays issuance of the tax card, escalate written request to the ETA central directorate; for NOSI discrepancies in wage declarations, submit corrected wage schedules and evidence of payroll contributions; administrative penalties for late tax registration are curable within 30 days with mitigating application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operating License for Registered Agent and Secretarial Services; Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (establishment licensing division), in coordination with the Civil Defense Department — Ministry of Interior.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an operating license application for a commercial service establishment under ISIC 8299. GAFI forwards the file to the Civil Defense Authority for a mandatory fire safety inspection of the office premises. After the inspection reports approval and payment of fire safety fees, GAFI issues an establishment operating license noting the services of registered agent, company secretarial and corporate facilitation. The license must be renewed annually in accordance with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate and GAFI incorporation certificate
Notarized lease or ownership document of the licensed office
Civil Defense fire safety certificate issued after inspection
List of business activities (restricted to ISIC 8299)
Identification of the responsible manager/storekeeper
Employee IDs and labor contract declarations
Fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Civil Defense identifies deficiencies, cure within 14 days and request a re-inspection; if GAFI refuses the activity code 8299, file a formal scope-of-business clarification with the GAFI Services Committee; repeated inactivity due to a missing document may be remedied by trader confirmation within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (Establishment Licensing Section) in cooperation with the General Organization for Industrial and Commercial Licensing under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Establishment Operating License for Business Support Services (Corporate Secretarial and Registered Agent Office) — Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Ministerial Decree No. 474 of 2020.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Low Environmental Risk) — this office-only activity is exempt from a full EIA study; the EEAA requires only the submission of Form B (Environmental Registration) and an administrative screening confirmation for a professional/administrative office use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The premises must comply with Prime Ministerial Decree No. 44/2000 discharge limits for wastewater entering municipal sewers; office operations must maintain indoor noise below 60 dB(A), implement paper and e-waste segregation per Law No. 202 of 2020 (Waste Management Regulation), and store no hazardous materials. Secretarial file disposal must be performed by licensed burning or shredding contractors with certificate of destruction retained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance Certificate (issued by the Civil Defense Directorate under the Ministry of Interior) requiring a valid fire extinguisher, adequate emergency exits, smoke detectors, and a documented evacuation plan; structural safety inspection by the Governorate's Construction Directorate for buildings older than 10 years; occupational safety clearance under the Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 with general first-aid kit, well-lit ventilation and ergonomic workstations for clerical employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official e-services and clearance portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg and e-invoicing platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must first be incorporated and licensed with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry, then apply to the competent ETA office for the Tax Card (TIN) and, separately, for VAT registration via the ETA online portal or designated service center. Nonresident entities with an Egyptian taxable establishment must appoint a local tax representative and obtain the relevant ETA registration number before issuing invoices; standard issuance takes approximately 5-15 working days from submission of commercial registry extract, resolution, amended contract, lease documentation, licenses, and identity documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide taxable profits; foreign shareholders' profit distributions are generally subject to dividend withholding at 10% under domestic law, with treaty relief available where applicable).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No OECD-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Egyptian law. Available statutory elections include ministerial-approved tax group consolidation for wholly-owned Egyptian subsidiaries, cash-basis accounting for small taxpayers as permitted by the Income Tax Law, optional VAT registration for persons below the EGP 500,000 threshold, and special tax stabilisation and incentive election mechanisms for entities registered under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2023)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 (annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services; mandatory registration is required before exceeding the threshold; persons exclusively exporting zero-rated supplies may register for VAT refund purposes; imported services are subject to reverse-charge VAT regardless of threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA e-invoicing and e-receipt system: near real-time fiscal clearance through the Egyptian Tax Authority's Innovex e-invoice platform; ERP-to-ETA API integration using XML/JSON structured files, a unique invoice UUID, and a machine-readable QR/ASCII stamp. All VAT taxpayers under the phased mandate must obtain an ETA clearance code for every invoice and receipt; non-compliant invoices are rejected and remain non-valid for local tax deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically removed from Egypt under customs supervision, including goods transported to free zones for future re-export, qualify for the 0% VAT rate where export documentation proves actual movement. Services supplied to non-residents qualify for zero-rating when they are performed for the non-resident's benefit, are enjoyed outside Egypt, are invoiced in foreign currency, and the consideration is duly remitted into Egypt. Domestic consumption and unremitted proceeds invalidate the zero-rate claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form E1/E2) with official customs stamp and export number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier or freight forwarder
Inward Remittance Certificate for the export proceeds issued by the Egyptian bank
Original commercial invoice referencing the Egyptian Tax ID and export statement
International sales contract and proforma invoice coupled with final payment evidence
Packing list and container or shipment tracking record where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may reassess export zero-rating documents for up to five years after the tax period. Missing, false, or forged supporting documentation invalidates zero-rating, triggering immediate VAT assessment at the 14% headline rate, monthly late-payment surcharge, administrative fines of up to EGP 1,000,000 per invoice, and retrospective clawback of any refunds paid. Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes expose the exporter to criminal penalties under the Egyptian Tax Evasion Law, imprisonment, suspension or cancellation of VAT registration, cross-audit with customs and foreign exchange authorities, and inclusion in the ETA non-compliant taxpayer register.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – البنك المركزي المصري; foreign exchange policy is administered through the CBE Exchange Control Department and the Foreign Operations/Foreign Investment Departments, with statutory grounding in the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and its implementing decrees.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a market-managed floating exchange-rate regime following the 2022 liberalisation; the EGP is fully convertible on current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, freight, professional fees, and licensing royalties) where underlying commercial documentation is presented. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections, intra-group financing, and portfolio inflows, require ex-ante or ex-post CBE declaration via the inward-transfer declaration forms (Form 4 / Form 5 / electronic CBE declaration), and profit/dividend repatriation is conditional upon tax clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), audited financial statements, and the availability of USD liquidity in the interbank market. Withholding tax on dividend remittances is generally 10% (5% cash dividend or 10% non-cash distribution) unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty; there are no residual surrender quotas or parallel-market requirements, but banks will not honour repatriation unless the CBE file is marked 'registered' by the receiving licensed bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Decision No. 207 of 2022 and subsequent circulars (effective 26 October 2022 onward), exporters of goods must repatriate 100% of export proceeds through a CBE-licensed bank within 6 months from the bill-of-lading/airway-bill date; service exporters, including registered-agent and corporate-secretarial fee remitters, must repatriate 100% of receivables within 90 days from the invoice due date unless a documented exemption is granted by the CBE Foreign Operations Department. Proceeds must be credited to an export-subscription account at the receiving Egyptian bank and may be retained in original foreign currency where the exporter holds a foreign-currency account under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; conversion to EGP, where requested, is executed at the CBE interbank prevailing rate. Delayed surrender without prior CBE approval exposes the exporter to fines, denial of future import financing, and suspension of the establishment's exporter card.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EGP and USD Accounts
Operational Account (EGP current and USD foreign-currency)
Operational Account (EGP/USD/EUR current or savings; FX margin facilities)
Operational Account (EGP/USD) for corporate service providers
Operational Account (EGP/USD) with correspondent USD rails via HSBC parent

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore digital EMIs is LOW-to-MEDIUM. Egypt's Fintech Law No. 5 of 2022, together with CBE Decrees No. 22 of 2021 and No. 118 of 2022, requires any electronic-payment or digital-banking service operating on Egyptian soil to obtain a CBE fintech/Banking-Activity licence; a remote offshore EMI (e.g., UK/FCA or Lithuanian-licensed) may not open onshore settlement accounts directly and may only act as a downstream payment facilitator through a full-service CBE-licensed bank or a licensed Payment Service Provider (PSP) in Egypt. The legal arrangement must be structured as a 'bank agency / payment technical partner' model, requires a Data Localisation Compliant server footprint, and must be registered with the CBE's Central Payments Council; otherwise, the EMI is categorised as an unlicensed cross-border service and is subject to blocking under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Egyptian banks require physical attendance by at least one authorized director, shareholder, or the duly appointed signatory at the branch, accompanied by the company's original Commercial Registry, tax card, and company resolutions; full-remote opening is not recognised as a standard path. The CBE AML/CFT Instructions (Articles 6–9 of Law 80 of 2002 and Unified E-KYC Rules of 2021) permit e-KYC only through a CBE-registered electronic-identity verification service provider and only for low-risk natural persons; for a Non-Resident corporate entity engaged in 'statutory corporate secretarial and registered-agency services', the bank's onboarding committee generally imposes enhanced due diligence (EDD), which includes an in-person interview with the UBO or a senior officer holding a written power of attorney, a notarised board resolution, legalised certificates on the parent-company existence, and a physical presence inspection of the registered office. Failure to make physical appearance within 60 days of account approval triggers account suspension.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Beneficial-ownership opacity across a portfolio of third-party offshore clients (professional intermediary risk under DNFBP classification and Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 22).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete UBO register (in Arabic and English) with certification of true-ownership attestation signed by the UBO; certificate of legal-existence and good-standing from GAFI Commercial Registry No. 8299/2000; copy of the AML Law 80/2002 compliance manual and the internal CDD procedure; a client-by-client list showing source-of-funds evidence, professional engagement letters, and confirmation that no client is a shell beneficial owner without underlying economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions and high-risk jurisdictional linkage (remittance beneficiaries or senders located in Sudan, Syria, Libya, Iran, Russia, Yemen, or territories subject to OFAC/EU/UN sanctions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a daily snapshot of sanctions screening of all clients against CBE-compiled sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, and UK OFSI; bilateral agreements or neutral counter-party business with evidence that services are limited to administrative corporate-legal functions; sworn declarations that the entity never processes payments on behalf of sanctioned persons; and an escrowed legal-professional privilege policy to protect client confidentiality without defeating disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Disproportionate low-value, high-frequency cross-border wires inconsistent with secretarial fee schedules (money-laundering layering and trade-red flag patterns).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ERP-extracted client lifecycle ledger showing issued invoices matched to payment references; detailed fee schedules per registered-agent package; trial balances and audit trail certified by an Egyptian CPA; three years of audited financial statements; and a bank-furnished 'source of funds' declaration template completed and signed by each material client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Statutory-licence insufficiency and lack of a recognised local professional licence to act as a Registered Agent / Company Secretarial Office under Egyptian Companies Law 159/1981 and GAFI Investment Law 72/2017.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the GAFI investment-services licence under Annex 5 with activity line 'Management and in-house company-secretarial services' (ISIC 8299); the municipal commercial-operating licence; CBE-undisturbed evidence of compliance under the Egyptian Secretaries and Corporate Governance Code; the professional indemnity insurance policy covering negligence in statutory filing and diligence; proof of registration in the FRA auxiliary database for non-banking ancillary services, if applicable; and a copy of the appointment of a statutory auditor under Law 159/1981 Article 17.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the EG LLC treasury op-co, all inbound foreign shareholder capital injections must move exclusively via SWIFT MT103 (for normal receipts) or SWIFT MT202/202COV (for bulk/back-to-back settlements) from the parent entity's bank account to the fee-earning operational account at the designated Egyptian tier-1 bank. The wire must carry the purpose code corresponding to Egypt's IMF BPM6 classification for 'Equity injection / Direct Investment' – CBE Form 8 (Inward Transfer Declaration) – and must include a clear reference to the GAFI investment-file number; the receiving bank will complete the e-registration with the CBE and issue an 'Inward Transfer Certificate' within 5 banking days. Funds routed in foreign currency must be either surrendered to EGP at the CBE interbank rate (subject to the bank's USD supply position) or kept in the company's designated USD foreign-currency account; no deferred conversion is permitted after 12 months, and the capital stock must be reflected in the capital escrow (under-subscription) account and the Commercial Registry announcement before any operational drawdown. Strictly verify that the remitter name matches the shareholder record at GAFI; mismatched remittances will be quarantined under the CBE's suspicion-surveillance rules and require an amendment filing before release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the company's professional services (including monthly retainer invoices to non-resident clients and supplier payments for fintech platform fees) clear through the CBE-licensed bank's correspondent network using (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account invoices, (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT707 for documentary commercial Letters of Credit where a goods-linked contract is embedded in the service supply, and (iii) Egyptian RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement) for same-day EGP legs. Each outward transfer must attach a stamped commercial invoice, the exchange-control 'Form 6' (for remittances above EGP 500,000 equivalent per transaction) or electronic e-Form submission, and, when paying a foreign supplier of other services, a landside tax certificate confirming no ETA withholding obligation is outstanding. Where a proportion of the company's revenue is received in USD and disbursed in USD, the treasury must maintain a segregated foreign-currency account and a designated USD correspondent drawing line; disbursement of foreign currency is nonetheless capped at the cumulative approved FX position reported to the CBE on a monthly basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards – onshore, CBE-licensed commercial banks only; supported by genuine underlying trade/invoice positions, tenors generally 1–12 months, executed under ISDA/CEMA master agreements.
FX Swaps (spot/forward rollover) – permissible for residential corporates as balance-sheet hedges against EGP depreciation when matched to specific current-account cash flows.

Cross-Currency Swaps (EGP/USD or EGP/EUR) – available with CBE-authorised money-centre banks for asset-liability matching and dividend-remittance shielding, requiring prior CBE no-objection notification, capacity under the Financial Regulatory Authority swap guidelines, and minimum ticket in excess of USD 500,000.

FX Options – permitted for non-speculative trade-flow hedging on a covered-underlying basis for banks licensed in Egypt; all premium and settlement flows are captured through the CBE reporting system.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing EGP – NOT permissible for Egyptian resident corporates under CBE rules; available only through international banking desks (London, New York, Dubai) to non-resident counterparties, and consequently cannot be booked in Egypt without a CBE security-dealing licence exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Unified Commercial Registry – General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of issuance; renewal must be completed before expiry, typically within 30 days prior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fee of EGP 500 per month of delay; continued non-renewal results in suspension of commercial registration and administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the company's fiscal year-end (March 31 of the following year for December 31 fiscal year-ends)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine for late filing of EGP 400–1,000; repeated failure may lead to administrative strike-off and blocking of commercial registry transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of the year following the tax year (fiscal year ending December 31); extension available to June 30 for audited financials on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 3% of tax due per month (maximum 60% of total tax); failure to file after notice may incur criminal fines and an administrative freeze of company bank accounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required where paid-in capital exceeds EGP 250,000, where the number of partners exceeds 10, or where gross annual turnover exceeds EGP 10,000,000. Smaller LLCs may dispense with audit only upon unanimous written consent of all partners.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not currently mandate a separate public UBO registry. Any share transfer must be entered in the register of members, notarized, and filed with GAFI within 30 days. In addition, registered agents are required to update their AMLR client files with current beneficial ownership details annually and retain those records for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Entities in Special Economic Zones and certain Free Zones may benefit from a 5-year tax holiday; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 provides a 50% deduction of investment costs for priority sectors; small enterprises may qualify for reduced rates under the Small and Medium Enterprise Income Tax Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance payments in March, June, and September)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, the final return and settlement are due by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number (TIN) and legal name of the LLC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian TIN issued at incorporation; non-resident directors must ensure the local licensed representative holds a valid power of attorney.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match the Egyptian fiscal year unless an alternate period has been approved by the ETA; non-resident shareholders should align records with the audited financials of the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and fees from registered agent and secretarial services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source revenues; income of a non-resident owner derived without a permanent establishment in Egypt is not normally chargeable to this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses (salaries, rent, professional costs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by tax invoices and contracts; intercompany charges paid to foreign entities must comply with arm's length transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutory adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident owned LLC, taxable profit must be determined solely on the Egyptian establishment's activities; foreign head-office overheads are deductible only if allocated under approved TP policies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable corporate tax rate and computation of headline tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 22.5%; non-resident shareholders must not apply treaty rate reduction to the LLC's own income; withholding-tax consideration arises separately on dividend distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a monthly penalty of 2% of the tax due (minimum EGP 1,000; maximum 100% of tax). Unpaid tax also draws daily interest computed as the Central Bank of Egypt lending rate plus 2% per annum. Failure to e-file can trigger additional administrative fines up to EGP 50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid by Egyptian LLCs to resident and non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit a written treaty-relief application to the ETA International Taxation Department before the distribution, attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, provide a beneficial ownership declaration, and obtain an advance tax-exemption certificate; otherwise, the 10% statutory rate is withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: 20% on royalties, 20% on interest. Under many Egyptian DTAs, royalties range from 10% to 20%, interest ranges from 10% to 15%, and interest paid to approved governmental entities may be exempt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 20,000,000 aggregate value of controlled transactions in a fiscal year; above this threshold the taxpayer must prepare and file a Local File and Master File with the annual return, together with a summary TP declaration.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not issue standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, Egyptian GAAR, and beneficial ownership rules require the LLC to maintain real local presence (office, staff, and decision-making) and to demonstrate substantive commercial activity. A pure letterbox entity is denied treaty benefits and may be recharacterized as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of client fees, invented expenses, forged supplier invoices, or using two ledgers to suppress taxable income in the registered-agent LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 91 of 2005, article 133, imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax; the ETA also recovers the full tax deficiency plus delay interest of the Central Bank rate plus 2% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct false returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties. Courts may pierce the corporate veil, order personal assets seized, and impose a travel ban on the managing directors until all tax liabilities are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LLC as a conduit or letterbox with no employees, no office, and no genuine business decision-making, solely to channel dividends or royalties abroad while claiming Egyptian treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may deny DTA relief, reassess the company on a look-through basis, impose 22.5% corporate tax on the entire non-resident-derived income, and apply fines of up to 200% of the avoided tax. GAFI may also strike the entity from the commercial register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally benefit from the sham arrangement can be held personally liable for the additional tax and penalties; criminal courts may impose imprisonment and passport seizure, and a re-entry ban for repeat offenders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct client due diligence, absence of a beneficial ownership register, no designated AML compliance officer, and non-reporting of suspicious transactions while acting as a corporate secretarial or registered agent service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80 of 2002, fines range from EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; the entity's operating license may be revoked by GAFI and the entity blacklisted from providing registered-agency services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML violations they knowingly allowed. Penalties include criminal imprisonment, travel bans, freezing of personal bank accounts, and civil restitution for client losses arising from sanctioned activities.
